title: What a class judgment decides
summary: A properly conducted class judgment can bind absentees, but its preclusive scope depends on the claims and issues actually resolved and on legitimate representation.
notes: A loss on a class-wide theory is not necessarily a finding that no class member suffered an individual wrong. Inadequate representation also raises an independent barrier to binding absentees.

sections.Meaning: A properly conducted class judgment can bind absentees, but its preclusive scope depends on the claims and issues actually resolved and on legitimate representation.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the class claim, the specific issue determined, and any individual claims left unresolved. Cooper distinguishes a general pattern of discrimination from individual discriminatory decisions.
